themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% increase (z-score: 7.78)—suggesting either a discrete event or coordinated illegal activity affecting Crown Heights' urban canopy.
evidence: 6 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 7.78 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Highest-ranked spike by recency and severity in the district
reporting_angles: On-the-ground canvassing to identify damaged trees and locate common characteristics (age, species, location pattern)
Interview Parks Department and 311 operators about whether spike is tied to single event (storm, construction, arson) or trend

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped to 92 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 51 per week—an 80% spike (z-score: 6.23)—with a concurrent 254% spike in dirty condition complaints 3 weeks ago, suggesting a systemic sanitation or waste management breakdown.
evidence: 92 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 51 weekly average (80% spike, z-score: 6.23)
Dirty condition complaints at 85 three weeks ago vs. 24 baseline (254% spike, z-score: 4.98)
Convergence with CB budget requests for building inspector expansion, suggesting chronic code enforcement shortfall
reporting_angles: Inspect specific blocks flagged by 311 to document conditions and patterns (residential vs. commercial, waste management failures)
Interview Sanitation Department about staffing, route changes, or equipment issues affecting Crown Heights specifically

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 28 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 7.4 per week—a 280% increase (z-score: 4.77)—indicating a sudden influx of Ubers, Lyfts, or unlicensed livery creating congestion, noise, or safety hazards.
evidence: 28 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average (280% spike, z-score: 4.77)
Timing suggests sudden market shift or external event (ride-share promotion, loss of parking, transit disruption)
Overlaps with ongoing illegal parking spike (2,142 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Map complaint hotspots (likely near subway stations, commercial areas, venues) to identify driver congregation zones
Interview TLC about licensing changes, enforcement activity, or ride-share market shifts in Brooklyn in past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Animal Activity in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal in a park complaints spiked to 6 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week—an 860% increase (z-score: 6.27)—raising questions about wildlife incursion, pest control failures, or seasonal migration.
evidence: 6 animal in park complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score: 6.27)
Convergence with CB budget requests for park building/access improvements
Potential connection to unsanitary conditions spike (food waste attracting wildlife)
reporting_angles: Document which parks are affected and what species are reported to assess public safety risk
Interview Parks Department about wildlife management protocols and whether sanitation issues are attracting animals

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints peaked at 14 THREE WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 3.5 per week—a 300% increase (z-score: 7.0)—pointing to possible mold, HVAC failures, or construction dust in residential buildings.
evidence: 14 indoor air quality complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 3.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 7.0)
Timing (early spring) suggests seasonal mold outbreak or heating system end-of-season failures
Convergence with heat/hot water complaints (3,714 over 90 days, highest category)
reporting_angles: Survey residents of affected buildings to identify commonalities (age, landlord, HVAC system type)
Cross-reference with HPD housing violation data to assess whether buildings have chronic heat/water or mold histories
